title: Connecting and hedging in speech
focus: ashole, borong, tobuo, jodio, jehetu, tachhara, mane, ontoto, sombhoboto, hoyto, nischoi, bisheshoto, onnodike, sotti bolte, ja-i hok, jemon, naki
body:
A heritage speaker's Bengali often sounds like a chain of short statements joined by ar and kintu. Adult speakers link and soften ideas with discourse words: ashole to explain, hoyto to hedge, tobuo to concede, ja-i hok to move on. Learn these words with the sentence position they take, because most sit at the start of a clause.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ashole | আসলে | actually, the thing is |
| borong | বরং | rather, instead |
| tobuo | তবুও | even so, still |
| jodio | যদিও | although |
| jehetu | যেহেতু | since, given that |
| tachhara | তাছাড়া | besides |
| mane | মানে | I mean |
| ontoto | অন্তত | at least |
| sombhoboto | সম্ভবত | probably |
| hoyto | হয়তো | maybe |
| nischoi | নিশ্চয়ই | surely |
| bisheshoto | বিশেষত | especially |
| onnodike | অন্যদিকে | on the other hand |
| sotti bolte | সত্যি বলতে | to be honest |
| ja-i hok | যাই হোক | anyway |
| naki | নাকি | apparently |

## Which word?

**hoyto vs sombhoboto vs nischoi.** These form a scale of certainty: hoyto (maybe), then sombhoboto (probably), then nischoi (surely). In casual talk "mone hoy" often replaces sombhoboto.

**jodio vs tobuo.** jodio opens the first clause ("although X"). tobuo opens the second ("still Y"). They often appear together: jodio X, tobuo Y.

**kintu vs tobe vs oboshyo.** kintu is a plain "but". tobe is softer and often introduces a condition. oboshyo adds a caveat after you have made your point.

**karon vs jehetu.** karon gives the reason after the main clause. jehetu gives it first and sounds more deliberate.

**bisheshoto vs bishesh kore.** Same meaning. bishesh kore is more conversational.

## Examples

- ashole ajke ektu byasto, kal kotha boli?: Actually I'm a bit busy today, can we talk tomorrow?
- jodio chakri-ta bhalo, tobuo ami khushi na: Although the job is good, I'm still not happy
- borong tumi-i ekbar or songe kotha bolo: Why don't you talk to him instead
- hoyto ami bhul, kintu amar mone hoy eta thik hobe na: Maybe I'm wrong, but I don't think this will work
- jehetu sobai ekmot, tai sidhanto-ta niye nilam: Since everyone agreed, we went ahead with the decision
- tumi nischoi shunechho, o naki biye korchhe: You must have heard, apparently she's getting married
- sotti bolte, ami ei byapare kichhu jani na: To be honest, I don't know anything about this
- ontoto ek-bar chesta kore dekho: At least give it one try
- ja-i hok, ja hobar hoyechhe, ebar samne takao: Anyway, what's done is done, now look ahead
- bhalo kotha, kal-er meeting-ta ki hochhe?: Oh by the way, is tomorrow's meeting still on?

cards.English: actually / the thing is (correcting or explaining)
cards.Example: ashole ami bhulei gechhilam: Actually, I completely forgot
cards.Notes: The most common softener before an excuse or explanation. Not for surprise ('actually?!' = tai naki?).

cards.English: rather / instead (it would be better to)
cards.Example: taxi na niye borong metro-te chalo: Rather than a taxi, let's take the metro
cards.Notes: Suggests a better alternative. Also 'on the contrary': o raag kore ni, borong khushi hoyechhe.

cards.Example: onek bujhiyechhi, tobuo shunlo na: I explained a lot, and still he didn't listen
cards.Notes: Starts the second clause. tobu is the shorter spoken form.

cards.Example: jodio deri hoye gechhilo, o tobuo elo: Although it was late, she still came
cards.Notes: Starts the first clause, often paired with tobuo or kintu. Also tacked on after: 'jodio ami jani na' = though I don't know.

cards.Example: jehetu tumi age theke jano, tumi-i bolo: Since you already know, you tell them
cards.Notes: Sounds measured; casual speech just uses karon or ...bole (deri hobe bole). Often paired with tai/sehetu.

cards.Example: flat-ta dami, tachhara office theke-o dur: The flat is expensive, and besides it's far from the office
cards.Notes: Adds one more reason. tachhara + noun = except (tumi tachhara keu jane na).

cards.Example: ami jete chai, mane, jodi tomar osubidha na hoy: I want to go, I mean, if it's no trouble for you
cards.Notes: Also 'meaning': er mane ki? = what does this mean? A natural filler while you think.

cards.Example: tar mane tumi ashchho na?: So that means you're not coming?
cards.Notes: Draws a conclusion from what the other person said; often a question.

cards.Example: ontoto ek-ta phone to korte parte: You could at least have called
cards.Notes: Both 'at a minimum' (ontoto doshta) and 'if nothing else'.

cards.Example: sombhoboto kal brishti hobe: It'll probably rain tomorrow
cards.Notes: Sounds a bit careful or formal; in casual talk people often say mone hoy (I think).

cards.Example: hoyto o bhule gechhe: Maybe she forgot
cards.Notes: Weaker than sombhoboto. Also a polite hedge: hoyto ami bhul, kintu... = I might be wrong, but...

cards.Example: tumi nischoi khub klanto: You must be very tired
cards.Notes: Guessing confidently about someone else. As a reply it means 'of course!' (nischoi, asho).

cards.Example: Kolkata-r khabar, bisheshoto mishti, darun: Kolkata food, especially the sweets, is amazing
cards.Notes: bishesh kore is the more spoken equivalent; bisheshoto sounds polished.

cards.Example: chakri-ta bhalo, onnodike maine kom: The job is good, but on the other hand the pay is low
cards.Notes: ulto dike means 'the opposite way' (ulto dike bhabo = think of it the other way round); onnodike is the standard contrast.

cards.Example: sotti bolte, cinema-ta amar bhalo lageni: To be honest, I didn't like the movie
cards.Notes: Fuller form: sotti kotha bolte ki. Softens a disagreeable opinion.

cards.Example: ja-i hok, ekhon kaaj-er kotha-e ashi: Anyway, let's get down to business
cards.Notes: Closes a tangent. Also 'whatever happens': ja-i hok na keno = no matter what.

cards.Example: kichhu jinish, jemon chal-dal, dam berechhe: Some things, like rice and lentils, have gone up in price
cards.Notes: Also 'like / the way': jemon bolechhilam = as I said. udahoron-sorup is the formal 'for example'.

cards.English: of course / mind you (adding a caveat)
cards.Example: o bhalo chhele, oboshyo ektu ragi: He's a good guy, though he's a bit short-tempered
cards.Notes: Adds a qualification after a statement. oboshyo-i = certainly (formal).

cards.Example: jete pari, tobe deri hobe: I can come, but I'll be late
cards.Notes: Gentler than kintu; introduces a condition or reservation. Also 'then' in old-fashioned speech.

cards.English: suppose / say (for the sake of argument)
cards.Example: dhoro chakri-ta pele, ki korbe?: Say you get the job, what will you do?
cards.Notes: Imperative of dhora (to hold); dhore nao = assume. dhoro is also a filler for estimates (dhoro panch hajar).

cards.Example: jotodur jani, o ekhon Bangalore-e: As far as I know, he's in Bangalore now
cards.Notes: Puts a hedge on information; jotodur mone porchhe = as far as I remember.

cards.English: most importantly / the biggest thing is
cards.Example: flat-ta sundor, ar sobcheye boro kotha, bhara kom: The flat is nice, and most importantly, the rent is low
cards.Notes: Used to land the strongest point at the end of a list.

cards.English: in a way / from one angle
cards.Example: ekdik theke bhalo-i holo: In a way, it worked out for the best
cards.Notes: Concedes a point partially; ekdik theke dekhte gele = if you look at it one way.

cards.Example: bhalo kotha, tomar boi-ta ferot dite bhule gechhi: Oh, by the way, I forgot to return your book
cards.Notes: Very Kolkata; literally 'good point'. kotha prosonge is the more formal 'by the way'.

cards.Example: o naki chakri chhere diyechhe: Apparently he's quit his job
cards.Notes: Placed after the subject for reported info. At the end of a question it means 'or': cha khabe naki coffee?

cards.English: you could say / so to speak
cards.Example: bola jay, o-i ei business-ta dar koriyechhe: You could say she's the one who built this business
cards.Notes: Softens a claim; bola jay na = you can't say / hard to say.

cards.Example: ha, ki jeno bolchhilam? o, flat-er kotha: Right, where was I? Oh, about the flat
cards.Notes: jeno marks trying to remember (or nam-ta ki jeno = what's his name again).

cards.Example: raag koro na, ami seta bolte chaini: Don't be angry, that's not what I meant
cards.Notes: Add amake bhul bujho na (don't get me wrong) to soften further.
